nodes.summary: The decision problem DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when bitstring decoding of $x$ as a triple $(n, E, K)$ succeeds and returns an instance of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE that is both well formed and feasible; every bitstring that does not decode is rejected.
nodes.title: DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is feasible when there is a list $T$ of pairs of natural numbers such that $T$ is a sublist of $E$ (obtained by deleting entries and keeping the order), $T$ has no repeated entries, $T$ has exactly $n - 1$ entries, the graph of $T$ on $n$ vertices is connected, and for every vertex $v < n$ there is no sublist of $T$ with $K + 1$ entries each of which has…
nodes.title: Feasibility for DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE

nodes.summary: An instance of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the degree bound).
nodes.title: Instances of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE

nodes.summary: The decision problem DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE belongs to the class NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is well formed when $n > 0$, the list $E$ has no repeated entries, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, with the reversed pair $(v, u)$ not in $E$.
